about.title: How Squeezo works
about.lead: What Squeezo does with each image and how it checks that the difference cannot be seen.

how.title: Step-by-step usage

steps.title: Review
steps.text: Choose what is compressed and what is excluded.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download each image separately or everything in a zip.

how.drag: Drag the files into the box
how.hint: This is a demonstration: drag the files, select the ones you want and compress.

items.name: JPG, WebP and AVIF
items.text: Lowers the quality to the point where the difference stops being perceptible.

items.name: PNG
items.text: Reduces the color palette when the difference is not noticeable. In high quality it keeps every pixel.

items.name: GIF
items.text: Keeps the animation and reduces the weight of the file.

items.name: SVG
items.text: Removes scripts and unnecessary code, without changing its appearance.

items.name: ZIP
items.text: It is read in parts, so even a very large zip is explored immediately.

items.name: Videos and others
items.text: They are not processed: you are told which ones were left out.

steps.title: Reading
steps.text: The image is opened in the browser and checked for what it really is: its content, its dimensions and its format.

steps.title: Measurement
steps.text: It is compressed at several quality levels and each result is compared with the original, in brightness and in color.

steps.title: Selection
steps.text: The lightest version that passes the threshold of the chosen level is kept. If none weighs less, the original is kept.

steps.title: Verification
steps.text: Before the result is delivered, it is measured on the full image and not only on a sample.

band.title: A thousand images in a single browser tab.
band.text: The work is split across the cores of the processor and zips are read in parts, without loading them whole into memory. That is why a large zip is explored immediately.

facts.label: to read a zip of 1000 images

items.title: Content verification
items.text: Every file is identified by its content and not by its extension. A .jpg file that actually contains text is rejected.

items.title: Protection against malicious zips
items.text: Paths that try to leave the destination folder, password-protected entries and files that, once unpacked, far exceed the size they declare are rejected.

items.title: SVGs without scripts
items.text: Scripts and external links are removed from SVG files, and they are only shown as images, never as pages.

items.title: Protection of personal data
items.text: JPG and PNG files lose their hidden data, such as the camera model and the location, unless it is requested to keep it.

items.a: Not visibly, at the recommended level. Squeezo compresses each image at several quality levels, compares each result with the original in brightness and in color, and only accepts the version whose difference cannot be seen at a glance. If you need maximum fidelity, the "High quality" level demands differences that are imperceptible even when zooming in, in exchange for a smaller weight reduction.

items.q: Do the dimensions of the image change?
items.a: No. Width and height stay the same, unless you turn on the dimension limit in the settings. In that case only the images that exceed the chosen limit are reduced, and their proportions are kept.

items.q: How much is the weight reduced?
items.a: It depends on each image. In tests with photographs, the recommended level reduced the weight by roughly 55% to 80%, and by more than 90% in PNG screenshots. Images that were already well optimized are left unchanged and you are told so.

JPG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF (animated too), SVG and BMP. TIFF and HEIC are processed only in browsers that can read them. GIF and SVG files always keep their format, and animated PNG, WebP or AVIF images are left unchanged so the animation is not lost.

items.q: What happens to videos and other files inside a zip?
items.a: They are skipped, and you are told how many there were and of what kind. Executables are dropped for safety. Squeezo only compresses images.
Up to 1000 images per zip and up to 50 megapixels per image are accepted. These limits protect the memory of the browser and prevent the device from being overloaded.

items.q: Are my files sent to any server?
items.a: No. All processing takes place in your own browser. No file is sent to a server and no account is needed. The only thing sent, when a compression finishes, is the number of images reduced, for the global counter on the About page.

items.q: What happens if I reload the page or close the tab?
items.a: Your progress is kept. The session is saved in the browser and, when you return, it is restored exactly as it was, even if a compression was halfway through, which resumes automatically. The "Clear" button deletes that data.

items.q: Are the camera data and the location kept?
items.a: By default they are removed from JPG and PNG files. If you need to keep them, you can turn that option on in the compression settings.

p: Squeezo works entirely in the browser. Images, folders and zip files are never sent to a server, and no registration or personal data is needed to use the tool.

Files are read and processed on the user's device, using the resources of its own processor. Squeezo receives no copy of them, does not analyze them remotely and does not share them with third parties.

Squeezo uses the browser's storage to save the working session, the chosen preferences (language, theme and compression settings). This data does not leave the device, is not tied to any identity and can be deleted at any time with the "Clear" button or from the browser settings.

Squeezo keeps a counter with the total number of images compressed by everyone who uses it, and the figure is shown on the About page. When a compression finishes, the browser sends only the number of images reduced, with no files, names or content. To prevent abuse, the IP address is converted into a short fingerprint that is kept for one minute and then deleted. The counter is stored in Upstash, a database service used through Vercel.
There are no user accounts, tracking cookies, analytics or advertising. Squeezo does not collect names, email addresses or any other data that identifies the user.

Photographs often include hidden data, such as the camera model or the place where they were taken. When a JPG or a PNG is compressed, that data is removed, unless the user turns on the option to keep it. If an image cannot be reduced, it is returned unchanged.

The site is hosted on Vercel, which may log technical data about each visit, such as the IP address, the date and the type of browser, under its own privacy policy. Those logs do not include the images or their content.

Squeezo includes no third-party scripts, fonts or resources: everything is served from the site itself. The links to the repository on GitHub and to the libraries used lead to external sites, which are governed by their own policies.
Squeezo examines the real content of every file, never runs anything that is added, rejects zips that pose a risk and removes scripts from SVG files.

Squeezo is a free, open source tool that reduces the weight of images, folders and zip files directly in the user's browser. It requires no registration or user account, and it includes no paid features.

The tool must be used only with images over which the user has the right of use. It is forbidden to use it to process unlawful content or content that infringes the rights of third parties, and to attempt to alter its operation, bypass its limits or use it for purposes that harm other people.

Files remain the property of their owner. Squeezo does not receive them, does not store them on servers and does not share them, because all processing takes place in the browser itself. The tool never modifies the originals: it creates compressed copies that are downloaded separately.

To avoid losing progress, the working session is saved in the user's browser storage, including the files added and the results obtained. That data stays on the device until "Clear" is pressed or the site data is deleted from the browser settings. On shared devices it is recommended to clear the session when finished.

Squeezo aims for the difference between the original and the compressed image not to be perceptible at a glance, and it verifies each result before accepting it. However, no lossy compression guarantees a result identical to the original, and the effect may vary depending on the image and the chosen level. Higher compression levels, format conversion and dimension reduction may produce visible differences. It is recommended to review the results with the comparison view and to always keep the original files.

To protect the operation of the browser, limits apply: up to 1000 images per zip, up to 50 megapixels per image and a maximum weight per file. Files that are not images, password-protected files, executables and files that pose a security risk are excluded from processing. The TIFF and HEIC formats can only be processed in browsers that support them.
